Invoke-ListDBCache.Description:
Retrieves cached tenant data from the CIPP reporting database (CippReportingDB). This is the fastest
and most efficient way to query tenant data across single or multiple tenants. The database is populated
nightly by background cache jobs, so data is typically at most 24 hours old.

Required query parameters:
  - tenantFilter: The tenant domain or 'AllTenants' to query all managed tenants.
  - type: The cache collection to retrieve (e.g. Users, Groups, Mailboxes, Devices, etc.).

Use type=_availableTypes to discover which cache collections exist for a given tenant. Omitting the
type parameter also returns the available types.

PERFORMANCE GUIDANCE: For AllTenants queries or any bulk/cross-tenant data retrieval, prefer
ListDBCache over calling individual endpoints (e.g. ListUsers, ListGroups, ListMailboxes) directly.
Individual endpoints make live API calls per tenant which is significantly slower and may hit
throttling limits. ListDBCache reads pre-cached data from Azure Table Storage and returns results
in seconds regardless of tenant count.

Recommended workflow for MCP tool selection:
  1. Call ListDBCache with type=_availableTypes to discover available cache collections.
  2. If the data you need exists as a cache type, use ListDBCache with that type.
  3. Only fall back to individual List* endpoints when you need real-time data for a single tenant
     or when the data is not available in the cache.

Common cache types include: Users, Groups, Mailboxes, Devices, ConditionalAccess, Applications,
IntunePolicy, CompliancePolicy, and many more. The exact set depends on what has been configured.

existing permissions) when it still inherits, and the role assignment is added with
addroleassignment.

Invoke-ListAdminPortalLicenses.Description: Retrieves license information from the Microsoft 365 Admin Portal for a tenant, including low-friction trial allotments.

Invoke-ListSites.Description: Lists SharePoint sites or OneDrive usage for a tenant. Requires a Type parameter (SharePointSiteUsage or OneDriveUsageAccount). Type=Adoption  -> getMicrosoft365CopilotUserCountSummary (per-product enabled vs active users)
Type=Trend     -> getMicrosoft365CopilotUserCountTrend    (per-date active/enabled users)

Invoke-AddEditTransportRule.Description: This function creates a new transport rule or edits an existing one (mail flow rule).

Invoke-ListQuarantinePolicy.Description: Lists quarantine policies configured in Exchange Online Protection, controlling end-user access to quarantined messages.

Invoke-ListApps.Description: Lists Intune managed applications for a tenant. Supports UseReportDB=true query parameter to retrieve cached data from the reporting database for significantly better performance, especially when querying AllTenants.

Invoke-ListRetentionCompliancePolicyTemp.Description: Lists saved retention compliance policy templates for deploying standardized retention configurations.

Invoke-ListSnoozedAlerts.Description: Lists alerts that have been snoozed (temporarily suppressed), filterable by cmdlet name. Returns snooze duration and scope details.

SharePoint external-store entry cannot be deleted (Microsoft deprecated

Invoke-ListWebhookAlert.Description: Lists configured webhook alert rules that trigger on specific audit log events.

Invoke-ListCopilotSettings.Description:
Lists the Microsoft 365 Copilot admin policy settings for a tenant, one row per setting,
with the current raw value and a friendly state (Enabled / Disabled / Not configured).

Invoke-ListAuditLogSearches.Description: Lists or creates Microsoft 365 Unified Audit Log searches for a tenant, with support for retrieving search results.

Invoke-ListMFAUsers.Description: Lists users and their MFA registration status for a tenant. Supports UseReportDB=true query parameter to retrieve cached data from the reporting database for significantly better performance, especially when querying AllTenants.

Invoke-ListSensitiveInfoTypeRulePackage.Description:
Returns the rule pack behind a custom Sensitive Information Type - the parsed rule configuration
(entities with confidence/proximity and their resolved regex/keyword/fingerprint detection) plus
the raw ClassificationRuleCollection XML - so the UI can show what a SIT actually detects.

Invoke-ListAuditLogTest.Description: Tests audit log webhook rules against a specific search to validate rule matching and alert triggering.

Invoke-ListSafeLinksPolicyTemplateDetail.Description: This function retrieves details for a specific Safe Links policy template.

Invoke-ListConditionalAccessPolicies.Description: Lists Conditional Access policies for a tenant with resolved display names for users, groups, applications, and locations.

Invoke-ListMailboxMobileDevices.Description: Lists mobile devices associated with a specific Exchange Online mailbox.

Invoke-ListContainerLogs.Description: Retrieves container logs for the CIPP backend process. Requires SuperAdmin access. Supports ReadLog, ListFiles, and snapshot actions.

Invoke-ListServiceHealth.Description: Lists active Microsoft 365 service health issues and advisories for a tenant or all tenants.

Invoke-ListNamedLocations.Description: Lists Conditional Access named locations (IP ranges and country-based locations) configured in a tenant.

Invoke-ListTenants.Description: Lists all managed tenants accessible to the current user, with support for cache clearing and tenant filtering. This is the primary endpoint for tenant enumeration.

Invoke-ListTenantAllowBlockList.Description: Lists Tenant Allow/Block List entries (senders, URLs, file hashes, IPs) from Exchange Online Protection.

Invoke-ListTenantDetails.Description: Retrieves detailed organization information for a tenant, including addresses, assigned plans, sync status, and custom properties.

Invoke-ExecDeleteSafeLinksPolicy.Description: This function deletes a Safe Links rule and its associated policy.

Invoke-ListAndroidEnrollmentProfiles.Description: Lists Android Enterprise enrollment profiles and hydrates token fields when Graph omits them from the list response.

Sets admin-level properties on a single SharePoint site (sharing, lifecycle, version
policy) through Set-CIPPSPOSite. Only whitelisted properties are accepted; enum values

to their numeric CSOM values here.

Invoke-ListOrg.Description: Retrieves the Entra ID organization profile for a tenant, including display name, addresses, and tenant metadata.

user list (which also catches guests who were granted membership but never signed in).
Every entry is classified against Entra: 'Entra B2B' (live Entra guest), 'Orphaned B2B'
(the Entra guest was deleted but SharePoint still references them) or 'SharePoint-only'
(legacy email-authenticated guest that never had an Entra object).

Invoke-ListAlertResults.Description:
Lists the currently-active fired alert items for a tenant, read from the
AlertLastRun table. AlertLastRun stores the items produced by the most recent
run of each scripted alert (Get-CIPPAlert*) after snoozed items have already
been filtered out, so this returns the active (non-snoozed) instances. Each
item is returned with a content preview/hash (matching the snooze format) and
the raw alert item so the frontend can snooze it via ExecSnoozeAlert.

Invoke-ExecGDAPTrace.Description:
Tests the complete GDAP (Granular Delegated Admin Privileges) access path for a user.

This function traces the access path from customer tenant → GDAP relationships → mapped security groups → user,
checking all 15 standard GDAP roles. It verifies whether a SAM user in the partner tenant has access to each
role through direct or nested group memberships across all active GDAP relationships for a customer tenant.

The function returns a role-centric view showing:
- For each of the 15 GDAP roles: whether it's assigned, whether the user has access, and the complete path
- Complete traceability: Role → Relationship → Group → User (including nested group paths)
- Broken path detection: identifies roles assigned but user not a member of the required groups

The output is structured as JSON suitable for diagram visualization, showing the complete access chain
regardless of which relationship provides each role.
